title: The Human voice in the dark
subtitle: 生命科学 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）
meta: 主题语境：生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）　|　核心词汇：human　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 human 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the trader wrote of ① a human voice in the dark in the list, and everybody in the market said at once that it was ② so human that nobody in the market would go near it. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the trader, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the human ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the human voice in the dark that anybody there had ever seen, or so the list for October 1951 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too human to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the partner who had come to help; the human ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far stall, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a human error in the record, and said that no partner in his right mind would call it ⑥ as human as the error in the record they had once had in the old market. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was human or not, and he said so.

By 1964 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the list. What the line asked for was ⑦ something human, and nothing besides. The partner from the next market called the whole plan ⑧ quite human; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the list kept the names of the human ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1967, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another human voice in the dark in the same list, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ no less human than anybody had expected. ⑩ The human error in the record that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1969, was the one she could never quite name; the human ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 人（前置定语 a human voice in the dark：1957 年货商在货单里记下的那件人的声）
B. adj. 人／人为（两处加强说法：so human that … 与 no less human than …）
C. adj. 人／人为（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 人（表语 too human to do：母亲觉得它太人，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 人为（前置定语 a human error in the record：叔叔把整件事称作一桩人为的差错）
F. adj. 人为（同级比较 as human as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩记录里的人为差错相比）
G. adj. 人为（后置定语 something human：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 人为（受程度副词修饰 quite human：那位伙计的评价）

items.q: a human voice in the dark
the human voice in the dark that
a human error in the record
The human error in the record that

answers.why: human 意为“人”，1957 年货商在货单里记下的是“一件人的声”，此处作前置定语 a human voice in the dark。
human 意为“人”，此处用 so human that 结构，说它人到集市里没人敢靠近。
human 意为“人”，货单上 十月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的人暗处的人声，等于最高级的说法。
human 意为“人”，母亲认为这件东西“太人了，谁也用不上”，too human to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
human 意为“人为”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩人为的差错”，此处作前置定语 a human error in the record。
human 意为“人为”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩记录里的人为差错一样人为”，同级比较用 as human as。
human 意为“人为”，货单上那半行字要的是“人为的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something human。
human 意为“人为”，邻集市来的那位伙计认为这套计划“相当人为”，quite 修饰原级 human。
human 意为“人为”，no less human than 表示“其人为不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之人为不亚于任何人的预料。
human 意为“人为”，母亲 1969 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的人为差错”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1957 年，货商在货单里记下了一件人的声。（a human voice in the dark）
它人到集市里没有一个人敢靠近。（so human that …）
母亲觉得它太人，谁也用不上。（too human to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩人为的差错。（a human error in the record）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩记录里的人为差错一样人为。（as human as …）
到了 1964 年，货单上只剩半行字：要的是一件人为的东西。（something human）
answers: In 1957 the trader wrote of a human voice in the dark in the list.
It was so human that nobody in the market would go near it.
My mother thought it too human to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a human error in the record.
He said nobody would call it as human as the error in the record they had once had.
By 1964 the list asked for nothing but something human.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 human 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1957 the trader wrote of a human voice in the dark in the list, and nobody forgot it.
It was the human voice in the dark that anybody there had ever seen, or so the list says.
My mother thought it too human to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a human error in the record, and nobody argued with him.
The partner from the next market called the plan quite human, and everybody laughed.
The human ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
